reasons: Section 20 contains an express Vendor defend-and-indemnify obligation covering third-party IP infringement/misappropriation of the Services or Deliverables (20.1) and Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2), matching limbs (a)-(d) of the model language.

Standard indemnity procedure is present (20.4: prompt notice with prejudice qualifier, cooperation at indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, settlement consent), and the infringement remedy ladder in 20.5 (procure, modify/replace, else terminate and refund) meets or exceeds the fallback.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized, plus Customer's own violation of law) with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination and Vendor instructions — consistent with the preferred position.

Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so the Vendor indemnity sits outside the liability cap, which is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap; the narrow cap base is correctly deferred to the limitation-of-liability rule to avoid double-flagging.

Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed, and the deterministic check confirms the Vendor IP indemnity is present; the rationale is accurate to the cited paragraphs.
